# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 712
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/712
- **Title**: fix(706): /model picker — one ChatGPT identity, reachable list top
- **Author**: vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit
- **Branch**: `fix/706-model-picker-dupes` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 7
- **Additions**: +511
- **Deletions**: -32
- **Created**: 2026-09-19T21:56:50Z
- **Updated**: 2026-09-20T07:48:11Z

## PR Description

Fixes #706

## What was wrong
- **Twin identities, both "current"**: ChatGPT OAuth derives the account name from the endpoint host (`chatgpt.com`) while the catalog/active provider is `chatgpt` — the /model provider step listed both rows, each marked `· current` (one via the active custom entry, one via the active provider).
- **Unreachable list top**: the menu window was a fixed 6 items regardless of terminal height; in short terminals the frame overran the glass and `_cropToGlass` (#503 guard) dropped rows from the TOP — the picker title and first items became selectable-but-invisible while the `↑ more` hint below stayed painted.

## Delivered
- `providerNameAliases` (`chatgpt.com` → `chatgpt`) + `canonicalProviderName()` in `custom_providers.dart`.
- Load-time migration: `CustomProviderRegistry` merges same-auth-domain records onto one (field union, reserved-named ghosts yield to non-reserved twins, named notes in `registry.mergeNotes`, surfaced at boot in `bin/fah.dart`).
- Alias-aware `registry.find()`.
- OAuth write path (`_applyChatGptOAuthCredentials`): resolves the existing same-domain record (base URL **or** canonical-name alias) and lands on it in place — no second record; the name prompt allows the alias-resolved target.
- Picker fold: `_modelProviderNames`/`_crossProviderCandidates`/`_providerModelCount`/`_openProviderModelPicker` group domain twins into ONE row (saved-entry spelling wins); the current marker compares canonical ids — exactly one `· current`.
- Viewport: `_menuWindow()` caps the window to the terminal height (`min(6, termHeight - 9)`, floor 1) so title + first items always land on the glass; tall terminals keep the classic 6-row window and hints.

## Tests (failing-first)
- `test/cli/agent_cli_provider_identity_test.dart` (3): load-merge of split records; full headless-OAuth repro of the owner screenshot → exactly one chatgpt identity row and exactly one current marker; OAuth onto an existing same-domain record mints no second record (blob lands in that record's key slot).
- `test/cli/fa_tui_picker_viewport_test.dart` (3): pgup lands title+first row on the glass in a 10-row terminal (was cropped: reproduced the exact reported frame); every row visible while walking a 12-item list at height 12; 24-row terminal keeps the legacy 6-row window + both hints.
- Regression zones green: agent_cli_model, agent_cli_provider, agent_cli_chatgpt_oauth, custom_providers, fa_tui, add_provider_picker, tui adapter/mouse/sync, aiin/copilot/env-preconfig/folder-model/compact/ext provider flows, codemie_sso_server, config_service — 325 passing.

## Gate note
`dart analyze` cannot run inside this `.worktrees/` lane under the current cube policy (analysis-server path canonicalization EPERMs — same family the chief flagged); the equivalent gates ran instead: harness Dart analysis server diagnostics clean on all 7 touched files, `dart format` applied, and every touched file compiled + exercised by the targeted suites above.

## Remaining (out of scope here)
- AC3's PTY-driven E2E variant (the model-level key-path tests cover the same interaction; the pty2 harness exists for a follow-up if wanted).
- Multi-row composer drafts while the picker is open can still squeeze the frame beyond the window cap (single-row draft — the picker reality — is covered).
- A `chatgpt-codex.com`-style future domains just need one map entry in `providerNameAliases`.

# gh-706: [BUG] /model picker: duplicate ChatGPT provider identities both marked current + list top unreachable ('↑ more' but no scroll)

## Description

## Goal — one provider identity, a fully reachable picker (v1, full create-goal rewrite)

One sentence: **every auth domain owns exactly one provider entry, and every model in the /model picker is reachable** — no `chatgpt` + `chatgpt.com` twins both marked "current", no `↑ more` rows the keys cannot reach.

Today (owner screenshot, 2026-09-19): the CLI /model picker lists both `chatgpt.com 1 model(s) · current` and `chatgpt 1 model(s) · current` — two identities for one ChatGPT auth — and the top of the list sits behind an `↑ more` marker that scrolling cannot actually reach. Why now: the ChatGPT OAuth flow (#614) is shipping and minting the duplicate identity in real configs; the picker clip is the #628 family still alive in this widget.

## Why this framing
- Two defects, one card, because both are picker-identity surface: the duplicate poisons "which provider am I on" (the same session later hit #705's switch bug), and the unreachable top makes the correct entry unselectable even when it exists.

## Architecture
- **Identity canonicalization** (subject: provider records): one canonical id per auth domain; an alias map folds `chatgpt.com` → `chatgpt` (and future domains). The OAuth write path RESOLVES aliases onto the existing entry instead of minting a new record. Invariant: *one provider id per auth domain across config, registry, and picker*.
- **Migration** (subject: already-split user configs): on load, duplicate same-domain records merge onto the canonical id — models and keys unioned, nothing dropped, a named note logged.
- **Picker viewport** (subject: the /model list widget): max height follows the live terminal size; ↑/↓ past the visible window scrolls so every entry is reachable. Invariant: *every listed entry is focusable by keys alone*. Codex reference for provider identity handling: https://github.com/openai/codex.

## Acceptance criteria (testable)
- **AC1** (RED, IT): fixture config with both `chatgpt` and `chatgpt.com` → load dedupes to one entry; the picker shows exactly one `· current`. (IT-D1)
- **AC2** (RED, IT): completing ChatGPT OAuth with an existing same-domain entry creates NO second record (alias resolution on the write path). (IT-D2)
- **AC3** (RED, E2E): /model with more entries than the window height — PTY test drives ↑/↓ past the fold; every entry reachable and selectable. (E2E-V1)
- **AC4** (REG): #614 auth-lands-in-list behavior, #628 clipping fixes, the #705 switch repro — all green. *Red REG blocks merge.* (REG-S1..S3)

## Test plan
### Test matrix
- `UT-D1..D3` — alias map resolution, merge rules (union of models/keys, conflict = canonical wins + note), canonical-id selection order: pure, no IO.
- `IT-D1..D2` — fixture configs through the real loader/registry (fakes, deterministic).
- `E2E-V1` — PTY: window height 12, 40 providers — every row focusable; selection lands on the canonical entry.
- `REG-S1..S3` — #614/#698-family auth flows, #628 pickers, provider switch path.

### Edge / border cases
- **E1** — split records carry DIFFERENT model lists: union, no loss; conflicting values resolve to canonical with a logged note.
- **E2** — the user's saved "current provider" points at the alias: resolves to canonical on load (no dangling pointer).
- **E3** — degenerate terminal (height < 3): picker still functional (min viewport + scroll), never a crash.
- **E4** — picker opened while a stream is in progress: list interaction never races the running turn's provider pointer.

## Non-goals
- Renaming/retheming the picker UI beyond the scroll fix.
- Cross-MACHINE identity sync (hub concerns stay out).
- Merging DIFFERENT auth domains (epam-copilot vs personal stay distinct — they are distinct).

## Open questions
- Canonical id spelling: `chatgpt` (current display) vs `chatgpt.com` (domain-shaped)? I lean `chatgpt` — shorter, already user-facing.

## References
#705 (same session's 400 — the downstream symptom), #614 (auth in one list), #628 (clipping family), codex: https://github.com/openai/codex.

Now let me deep-read the changed files. Key areas:

1. `custom_providers.dart` — the merge logic. Concerns:
   - `_mergedOnLoad` only unions `keyName` — but the ticket says "models and keys unioned" (E1: "union, no loss"). `CustomProviderEntry` has fields: name, apiType, baseUrl, modelId, keyName, maybe others. Unioning only keyName means modelId/baseUrl of the twin are dropped if survivor lacks them... actually only keyName union. What other fields exist? Need to read the class. If twin has a modelId and survivor has null modelId, survivor loses it — "nothing dropped" violated. Let me check.
   - `_mergedOnLoad` mutates entries in place (`_unionOnto` mutates survivor object) — the entries are CustomProviderEntry objects; but also the source list passed in `saved.customProviders` — the registry copies? Before: `entries = List.of(entries)` — copy of list. Now: `_mergedOnLoad(entries)` builds a new list of (potentially same) entry objects. The input `saved.customProviders` list itself isn't mutated (fine). But entry objects are mutated — they may be shared with config objects that get persisted. Actually mutation of survivor via _unionOnto mutates the entry that is in `saved.customProviders` too — but entries is supposed to be "a live, mutable list" — the previous version did `List.of(entries)` so the list was a copy but entries shared anyway. Fine.
   - `_loadMergeNotes` note says merged onto "first" — but when reserved-named ghost is dropped and non-reserved twin wins, the note names may mislead: e.g., source order [chatgpt (reserved ghost), chatgpt.com]; seen: chatgpt → id chatgpt; chatgpt.com → id chatgpt → note 'merged duplicate provider record "chatgpt.com" onto "chatgpt"' — but actually chatgpt.com is the SURVIVOR and chatgpt was dropped! The note is backwards/misleading. That's an important correctness/naming issue: the note says merged X onto Y where Y was dropped and X survived. Block-worthy? It's a user-facing message that's incorrect — IMPORTANT.
   - Also in `_mergedOnLoad`, when the reserved ghost came first and non-reserved twin comes later: `survivors[id] = _unionOnto(entry, existing)` — mutates `entry` (the later one) and replaces. OK. But if BOTH are reserved or both non-reserved, first wins — fine.
   - Merge notes: duplicates note text says "merged ... onto first" but if existing was reserved ghost and entry non-reserved, the survivor is entry not first. Yes, misleading note confirmed.
   - Another issue: merge only handles keyName union; entry has apiType, baseUrl, modelId, keyName fields. If ghost has baseUrl set and survivor's baseUrl is null... can baseUrl be null? Check class definition.

2. `bin/fah.dart`: `..mergeNotes.forEach(stdout.writeln)` — writes to stdout. In the CLI, stdout is the TUI/primary stream. Concern: in headless mode with `--output events` (HEP), stdout must stay pure JSONL — writing merge notes to stdout would corrupt the HEP stream! Check where this is in _runApp — is it before headless routing? Also `CliIO` contract: write = primary stream, writeln = diagnostics (stderr headless). Writing via `stdout.writeln` directly bypasses CliIO and could pollute machine-parseable stdout. Need to check context in bin/fah.dart line ~1885. Let me read.

3. `provider_commands.dart` `_applyChatGptOAuthCredentials`:
   - When target != null (alias-resolved existing record), they update modelId and keyName in place, but NOT `apiType` and `baseUrl`. If existing record was created with different baseUrl... probably fine.
   - `target..modelId = modelId..keyName = keyName` — keyName here: what is keyName in this scope? It's the entry's own slot. OK.
   - `_activeCustomName = name;` — name is the typed/fallback name. When landing on an existing target, `name` may differ from target.name? Actually find(name) — name is the resolved name from prompt; fallback = existing?.name. If the user types a NEW name, find(name) is null → add fresh. But wait: `registry.find(name)` is now alias-aware! If user types "chatgpt" as a new name intending... find('chatgpt') would return the chatgpt.com entry via canonical matching, so `target != null` → update in place. Hmm — but `name` typed is 'chatgpt' which is a reserved name... does the name prompt reject reserved names? `_askConnectProviderName` presumably rejects reserved names (clash with catalog). So typed 'chatgpt' would be rejected by the prompt. But what if a user types some OTHER alias? Only chatgpt.com→chatgpt in the map.
   - Subtle: after landing in place, `_activeCustomName = name` — if target found via alias (find returns entry with different name, e.g. find('chatgpt') returns 'chatgpt.com' entry), then `_activeCustomName` is set to 'chatgpt' which does not match the entry name. `_activeCustomName` semantics: name of active custom entry. Setting it to a name that isn't the entry's actual name could break `find` logic elsewhere or the "· current" marker (which compares `name == active`). Actually the current marker compares `name == active || canonicalProviderName(name) == currentId`. If active = 'chatgpt' but entry is 'chatgpt.com', `name == active` fails, but canonical compare with current provider covers it. But elsewhere `_activeCustomName` might be used for model memory rewriting ("/model rewrites the active entry's last-used model"). If code does `registry.find(_activeCustomName)` — find is alias-aware so it resolves. Probably OK but worth noting.
   - Also, when target != null: `name` could equal... if find returns via exact match, target.name == name (case-insensitive). If via alias, names differ. Then `_activeCustomName = name` is the alias, not the entry name. Consider: existing = entry named 'chatgpt.com'; fallback = 'chatgpt.com'; user accepts → name = 'chatgpt.com'; find('chatgpt.com') → exact → target.name = 'chatgpt.com'. Fine. Alias path via find only triggers when user types a different alias spelling. Reserved names rejected, so 'chatgpt' can't be typed... unless not rejected in this prompt variant with allowClash. allowClash: (clash) => clash == existing — the clash callback. Need to see _askConnectProviderName signature to verify clash is entry.

4. `fa_tui.dart` `_menuWindow`: `maxVisible = (termHeight - 9).clamp(1, 6)`. Magic number 9 hardcoded — the comment explains chrome rows. Potential mismatch: the picker footer "models-picker footer" — is footer only present for the models picker? If other pickers (slash menu?) lack the footer, the window is over-capped (minor). If termHeight is 0 or negative (unknown), clamp floor 1. OK. But `termHeight` — need to check it's the live height and updates on resize. Probably fine.
   - The comment says "progress indicator + frame rules + status (4), one input row, the menu title, both scroll hints, the models-picker footer" = 4+1+1+2+1 = 9. OK.

- `_entryForBaseUrl(registry, 'https://chatgpt.com/backend-api/codex')` → null (different baseUrl).

Note test 1 comment says "the union keeps the key slot and the last-used models" — but `_unionOnto` only unions keyName; the twin's modelId ('gpt-5') is DROPPED when the survivor has its own ('gpt-5-codex'). Also: the twin's key slot — survivor already has a keyName, so twin's keyName 'CHATGPT_OAUTH_CREDENTIALS' is dropped — but wait, CHATGPT_OAUTH_CREDENTIALS is the OAuth blob slot! If the ghost holds the OAuth credentials slot and survivor has its own keyName, the OAuth blob is orphaned (still in secure store but unreferenced). Scenario: ghost 'chatgpt' created by an earlier OAuth (blob in CHATGPT_OAUTH_CREDENTIALS), then a later OAuth minted 'chatgpt.com' with its own slot... actually chatgpt OAuth blob always lives in CHATGPT_OAUTH_CREDENTIALS per AGENTS.md. Conflicts keep survivor's keyName — if survivor's slot differs from twin's, one set of credentials becomes orphaned. Edge; conflicts must pick one. Note-worthy as part of the union observation. SUGGESTION.

{"content":"🚨 **BLOCKING: Merge notes are written to stdout — corrupts the HEP event stream and headless output**

```dart
customProviders: CustomProviderRegistry(saved.customProviders)
  ..mergeNotes.forEach(stdout.writeln),
```

`_runApp` also serves headless runs. With `--output events` (HEP v1, issue #155) stdout is a **strict JSONL stream** owned by `HepWriter` — the code right above this hunk says it verbatim: *"Stdout purity: deltas ride frames; diagnostics keep their channel"* (bin/fah.dart:1827-1830) and wraps `io` in `HepEventsIO` for exactly this reason. Any user whose saved config still carries a `chatgpt` + `chatgpt.com` split (the exact users this PR migrates) will get raw prose lines injected into the JSONL stream, breaking every server-side supervisor parsing it. Even plain headless `fa "prompt"` gets the note prepended to the answer stream.

The file already has the correct convention a few hundred lines up (bin/fah.dart:498):

```dart
void writeln(String text) =>
    headless ? stderr.writeln(text) : stdout.writeln(text);
```

Route the notes through `io`/stderr (or buffer them and emit through the CLI's diagnostic channel after `io` is built) instead of raw `stdout`.

{"content":"⚠️ **IMPORTANT: Merge note names the wrong survivor when the reserved ghost is listed first**

```dart
notes.add(
  'merged duplicate provider record "${entry.name}" onto "$first" '
  '(same auth domain)',
);
```

`_loadMergeNotes` assumes the FIRST-seen record is the survivor, but `_mergedOnLoad` has the reserved-ghost flip: for the config order `[chatgpt (reserved ghost), chatgpt.com]`, the survivor is **`chatgpt.com`** (non-reserved wins) and `chatgpt` is dropped — yet the note prints `merged duplicate provider record "chatgpt.com" onto "chatgpt"`, the exact opposite of what happened.

This note is the only audit trail of a migration that is persisted back to the user's config on the next save (the registry list is the live, persisted list), and these notes are now surfaced at every boot. Telling the user the wrong record survived sends them hunting for a `chatgpt.com` entry that no longer exists.

Two suggestions:
1. Emit the note from `_mergedOnLoad` itself, where the actual survivor is known — that also removes the duplicated detection pass (`_loadMergeNotes` re-implements the same grouping and can drift from `_mergedOnLoad`).

⚠️ **IMPORTANT: Alias landing ignores apiType/baseUrl — can overwrite an unrelated key slot and leave an inconsistent record**

```dart
final existing = registry != null
    ? (_entryForBaseUrl(registry, spec.defaultBaseUrl) ??
          _entryForCanonicalName(registry, spec.name))
    : null;
```

`_entryForCanonicalName` matches purely on the NAME (`canonicalProviderName(entry.name) == 'chatgpt'`). A user who hand-created an entry literally named `chatgpt.com` pointing at a **different** backend (a corporate proxy/relay, apiType `openai`, its own `keyName` slot) hits this path:

1. `existing` = the proxy entry → `keyName = existing.keyName` → `_storeProviderToken` **overwrites the proxy's stored key** with the ChatGPT OAuth blob (silent credential loss).
2. The in-place update below refreshes only `modelId`/`keyName` (lines 1416-1418) — the record keeps apiType `openai` and the proxy `baseUrl` while now holding Codex OAuth credentials that need the Responses-API dialect (`store: false`, `ChatGPT-Account-ID`). Switching to that entry later is broken in both directions.
3. `sameAccount = name == existing.name` is true, so the model pick is skipped for what may be a completely different account.

The doc comment ("may carry a variant base URL — landing on it is the point") shows this was considered, but the variant should still be constrained to the same auth domain: require `apiType == spec.name` (or a trailing-slash-normalized baseUrl match) before treating the record as the OAuth landing target, and/or refresh `apiType`/`baseUrl` on the target when landing. A proxy entry named `chatgpt.com` is exactly the kind of hand-edit this PR's migration is meant to clean up after.

⚠️ **IMPORTANT: The `-9` chrome reserve doesn't account for group-header rows — the top-crop bug survives for grouped menus**

```dart
final maxVisible = (termHeight - 9).clamp(1, 6);
```

The reserve covers title + both hints + the models footer, but `_menuReservedLines` (same file, ~line 530) counts one more row per visible **group header** (`_groupHeadersIn`). `_menuWindow` is shared by every menu, and the slash menu renders groups (`commands`, `skills` — see `slash_menu.dart`), the composer overlay uses `paths`. With a grouped menu in a short terminal the frame still overruns the glass by the header count and `_cropToGlass` (line ~2165) drops rows from the TOP again — the same #706/#628 defect this PR fixes for the (ungrouped) /model picker.

The height math already exists and stays in sync with the renderer precisely because it lives in one place (`_menuReservedLines`: *"the height math and the renderer must agree"*). Consider computing the cap from that same accounting — e.g. clamp the window so `1 + window + headers(window) + hints + footer <= termHeight - fixedChrome` — instead of hand-mirroring the row budget in a magic `9` that will silently rot the next time the frame chrome changes.

All required context — ticket description, PR diff, CI status, and related materials — has already been prepared in the `input/` folder. Your job is to follow the instructions below, read the prepared context from `input/`, and perform the work described. Do not ask for identifiers; the context is already available locally. ```mermaid flowchart TD G1["⚠️ Review Guidelines — evaluate against existing codebase patterns"] G2["Before reviewing, explore the project's code structure, architecture, and testing patterns"] G3["If AGENTS.md exists → READ it — defines coding styles to check against"] G4["Flag deviations from established patterns unless justified in PR description"] G1 --> G2 --> G3 --> G4 ``` # PR Review General Guidelines ## Review flow ```mermaid flowchart TD START([PR ready for review]) --> READ["1. Read input context:
instruction.md, ticket.md, pr_info.md,
pr_diff.txt, pr_files.txt, ci_failures.md,
ci_failures_full.log, pr_discussions.md,
pr_discussions_raw.json"] READ --> DIFF["2. Run diff checklist on pr_diff.txt"] DIFF --> FILES["3. Read full content of every changed file"] FILES --> CODEGRAPH["4. Use CodeGraph:
callers/callees of changed symbols,
search for sensitive patterns,
impact analysis"] CODEGRAPH --> DIMS["5. Evaluate review dimensions:
Security · Architecture/OOP · Code quality
Test coverage · Duplication · Backward compatibility"] DIMS --> SEVERITY["6. Classify each finding:
BLOCKING / IMPORTANT / SUGGESTION"] SEVERITY --> EXHAUST["7. Exhaustive pass:
re-read changed files,
surface ALL remaining issues"] EXHAUST --> OUTPUT["8. Write outputs:
pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Impact analysis (CodeGraph or grep fallback) Use CodeGraph to find "what could break": - `codegraph_callers` / `codegraph_callees` on modified public symbols - `codegraph_search` for: `PAT_TOKEN`, `secrets.`, `github.token`, `previousViewModel` - `codegraph_impact` before flagging architectural changes **If CodeGraph unavailable**, use grep and document it: ```bash grep -rn "changedFunctionName" --include="*.ts" . grep -rn "secrets\.\|github\.token" . ``` ## 5. Review dimensions Rate the PR across all relevant dimensions: | Dimension | What to check | |---|---| | **Security** | injection, unsafe interpolation, secret leakage, missing permissions, unsafe defaults | | **Architecture / OOP** | SRP, coupling, abstraction consistency, provider/repository boundaries | | **Code quality** | naming, complexity, error handling, logging, comments | | **Tests** | coverage for new/changed paths, meaningful assertions, no brittle string-only tests | | **Duplication** | copy-paste, duplicated logic across files, duplicated configuration | | **Backward compatibility** | public API changes, migration paths, default behavior | | **Performance** | unnecessary rebuilds, heavy sync operations, missing timeouts | | **Workflow / CI safety** | (when `.github/workflows/` changes) secret declarations, ref pinning, permissions, timeouts | ## 6. Severity classification Classify every finding before writing outputs: - **BLOCKING** — merge would cause a bug, security issue, data loss, or CI break. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. Outputs Write the standard review artifacts: - `outputs/pr_review.json` — structured data with `recommendation`, `summary`, `inlineComments`, `issueCounts` - `outputs/pr_review_general.md` — 1-2 paragraph general PR comment - `outputs/pr_review_comments/*.md` — one file per detailed inline comment **Inline comment lines must be present in the PR diff.** GitHub review threads can only be attached to added or context lines inside a diff hunk. If `pr_diff.txt` is truncated, run `git diff origin/{baseBranch}...HEAD` to locate the correct line numbers. Findings on unchanged code outside the diff belong in `outputs/pr_review_general.md`, not as inline comments. # AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/unattended), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.
- `lib/src/tools/checkpoint_tool.dart` — `checkpoint`/`rewind` tools:
  context hygiene for detours. `CheckpointRewindController` wraps
  `Agent.prepareNextTurn`, persists via host `CheckpointSessionSink`.
  Lifecycle (issue #286): a checkpoint is scoped to its detour — when the
  next `checkpoint` call finds it stale (a user turn arrived inside the
  detour, or the anchored span was rebuilt away by reload/compaction), it
  is auto-closed with a note + `checkpoint_auto_closed` session record
  instead of refusing; `rewind` semantics are unchanged.
- `lib/src/compaction/branch_summarization.dart` — `generateBranchSummary` +
  `navigateSessionTree` (use instead of `Session.moveTo` for tree
  navigation); summary is a `branch_summary` record on the entered branch.
- `lib/src/agent/tool_pairing.dart` — context pair-integrity (issue #85):
  `validateToolPairing` checks the wire-equivalent message sequence (orphan
  results, unanswered calls, duplicate ids, displaced results after
  same-role merges); `repairToolPairing` fixes the outbound payload only
  (drop orphan + note, synthesize interrupted results, hoist steering text
  after results, uniquify duplicate ids symmetrically on call+result).
  `agent_loop.dart` repairs before every request and retries once on a
  pairing-shaped provider 400 (`ToolPairingRepairEvent` is the audit
  trail); `_finishStreamed` stamps per-run position-counter ids
  session-unique; `auto_compactor.dart`'s `_localTrimFallback` routes the
  kept region through the same repairer.
- `lib/src/agent/image_registry.dart` — session image registry (issue
  #171): unique images ride a provider request exactly once; every other
  occurrence becomes a `[Image N]` text ref. `rewriteHistoryImages`
  rewrites the OUTBOUND payload only (session JSONL byte-identical);
  carriers `[{text:"[Image N]"},{image}]` anchor before the first
  referencing user message or after the tool-result run (never inside
  call/result pairs); the current user message rides images in place
  (I3), each in-place image carrying its `[Image N]` label (issue #195
  F3 — the model can cite what it sees); the per-request cap
  (`images.maxPerRequest`, default 20) drops current-first-then-newest
  with a drop notice (never silent; the app logs drops via `AppLog`,
  issue #195 F4); dangling refs (compaction, cap) resolve to `(image no
  longer available)`, and once a renumbering boundary exists (compaction
  summary, structured marker, local-trim note) AUTHORED history
  citations degrade to that note too — after renumbering an `[Image N]`
  may name a different image, so silent rebinding is never allowed
  (issue #195 F2; generated refs/labels stay content-keyed and fresh).
  Stateless per-request rebuild — determinism, compaction eviction and
  resume come free. Kill switch `images.registry: false` → byte-for-byte
  legacy shape. `agent_loop.dart` applies it in `_buildRequestContext`
  after `transformContext`, before tool-pairing repair.
- `lib/src/trajectory/` — the trajectory ledger core (issue #10): finalized
  session records project into an immutable `TrajectorySnapshot` through
  `TrajectorySnapshotBuilder.append`/`applyEvent` — streamed agent events
  land as synthetic rows keyed `turn\0step` (`u\0turn` for prompts) and are
  replaced when the real record lands; revision grows per append. Record
  kinds (closed set, `TrajectoryCellKind`): system, user, context,
  compacted, message, tool, subtool — a subtool is a
  `TrajectoryToolRecord.parentCallId != null`, which only hosts build
  directly (the builder never nests). Derived state folds once per
  snapshot: `deriveTrajectoryLayout` (turns of Message/Step groups +
  collapsible turn/assistant-run summaries), `deriveTrajectoryTimeline`
  (four modes — `sequence` equal-width slots, `duration` with idle gaps
  compressed out, `time` zero-width wall-clock markers, `actual` real gaps;
  three fixed lanes: 0 system/user/context, 1 message/compacted, 2 tools),
  `trajectoryTimelineFocusIndexes` (selection → visible ledger indexes),
  and `ThrottledTrajectorySearchIndex` (full-text; matches are stable
  record ids). `formatters.dart` holds the shared duration/token/throughput
  formatting; `trajectory_preview.dart` the bounded single-line previews;
  `trajectory_export.dart` the whole-snapshot JSON/Markdown exporters the
  header's copy menu uses. Tool records carry `startedAt` (real launch
  time, distinct from the projected position) so the Gantt/actual
  projections plot true spans. Outbound model requests persist for the
  ledger as hidden `model_request_summary` `CustomRecord`s — the CLI
  event handler (`agent_event_handler.dart`, emitted through
  `agent_cli.dart`) and the app's `AgentService` both buffer a
  `TrajectoryRequestDetail` per call and flush it onto the session
  record chain right before the assistant message, so replays see it
  ahead of the reply — and `TrajectorySnapshotBuilder` folds them into
  the message record's request detail (the Request tab).
  Consumers render, never re-derive: `packages/fa_ui`'s
  `lib/src/trajectory/` widgets and the CLI `/trajectory` family.
- `lib/src/cli/trajectory_commands.dart` (a `part of` `agent_cli.dart`) +
  `lib/src/cli/trajectory_tui.dart` — the read-only REPL family
  `/trajectory [view|cost|tail|inspect <n>]` (bare = `view`, capped at 200
  rows; `tail` follows the live session every 500ms) and the headless
  `fa trajectory <view|tail|cost|inspect> [sessionId] [--json] [--at N]`
  subcommand (`--at N` replays the snapshot as it stood at record N, view
  only). Session resolution: exact id > session-name match > most recent.
  Rendering is pure Dart in `trajectory_tui.dart` (no `dart:io`), shared by
  both entries; `bin/fah.dart` routes the subcommand.
- `lib/src/redact/` — laye…

- **Title**: fix(706): /model picker — one ChatGPT identity, reachable list top
- **Author**: vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit
- **Branch**: `fix/706-model-picker-dupes` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 7
- **Additions**: +511
- **Deletions**: -32
- **Created**: 2026-09-19T21:56:50Z
- **Updated**: 2026-09-20T07:48:11Z

## PR Description

Fixes #706

## What was wrong
- **Twin identities, both "current"**: ChatGPT OAuth derives the account name from the endpoint host (`chatgpt.com`) while the catalog/active provider is `chatgpt` — the /model provider step listed both rows, each marked `· current` (one via the active custom entry, one via the active provider).
- **Unreachable list top**: the menu window was a fixed 6 items regardless of terminal height; in short terminals the frame overran the glass and `_cropToGlass` (#503 guard) dropped rows from the TOP — the picker title and first items became selectable-but-invisible while the `↑ more` hint below stayed painted.

## Delivered
- `providerNameAliases` (`chatgpt.com` → `chatgpt`) + `canonicalProviderName()` in `custom_providers.dart`.
- Load-time migration: `CustomProviderRegistry` merges same-auth-domain records onto one (field union, reserved-named ghosts yield to non-reserved twins, named notes in `registry.mergeNotes`, surfaced at boot in `bin/fah.dart`).
- Alias-aware `registry.find()`.
- OAuth write path (`_applyChatGptOAuthCredentials`): resolves the existing same-domain record (base URL **or** canonical-name alias) and lands on it in place — no second record; the name prompt allows the alias-resolved target.
- Picker fold: `_modelProviderNames`/`_crossProviderCandidates`/`_providerModelCount`/`_openProviderModelPicker` group domain twins into ONE row (saved-entry spelling wins); the current marker compares canonical ids — exactly one `· current`.
- Viewport: `_menuWindow()` caps the window to the terminal height (`min(6, termHeight - 9)`, floor 1) so title + first items always land on the glass; tall terminals keep the classic 6-row window and hints.

## Tests (failing-first)
- `test/cli/agent_cli_provider_identity_test.dart` (3): load-merge of split records; full headless-OAuth repro of the owner screenshot → exactly one chatgpt identity row and exactly one current marker; OAuth onto an existing same-domain record mints no second record (blob lands in that record's key slot).
- `test/cli/fa_tui_picker_viewport_test.dart` (3): pgup lands title+first row on the glass in a 10-row terminal (was cropped: reproduced the exact reported frame); every row visible while walking a 12-item list at height 12; 24-row terminal keeps the legacy 6-row window + both hints.
- Regression zones green: agent_cli_model, agent_cli_provider, agent_cli_chatgpt_oauth, custom_providers, fa_tui, add_provider_picker, tui adapter/mouse/sync, aiin/copilot/env-preconfig/folder-model/compact/ext provider flows, codemie_sso_server, config_service — 325 passing.

## Gate note
`dart analyze` cannot run inside this `.worktrees/` lane under the current cube policy (analysis-server path canonicalization EPERMs — same family the chief flagged); the equivalent gates ran instead: harness Dart analysis server diagnostics clean on all 7 touched files, `dart format` applied, and every touched file compiled + exercised by the targeted suites above.

## Remaining (out of scope here)
- AC3's PTY-driven E2E variant (the model-level key-path tests cover the same interaction; the pty2 harness exists for a follow-up if wanted).
- Multi-row composer drafts while the picker is open can still squeeze the frame beyond the window cap (single-row draft — the picker reality — is covered).
- A `chatgpt-codex.com`-style future domains just need one map entry in `providerNameAliases`.

# gh-706: [BUG] /model picker: duplicate ChatGPT provider identities both marked current + list top unreachable ('↑ more' but no scroll)

## Description

## Goal — one provider identity, a fully reachable picker (v1, full create-goal rewrite)

One sentence: **every auth domain owns exactly one provider entry, and every model in the /model picker is reachable** — no `chatgpt` + `chatgpt.com` twins both marked "current", no `↑ more` rows the keys cannot reach.

Today (owner screenshot, 2026-09-19): the CLI /model picker lists both `chatgpt.com 1 model(s) · current` and `chatgpt 1 model(s) · current` — two identities for one ChatGPT auth — and the top of the list sits behind an `↑ more` marker that scrolling cannot actually reach. Why now: the ChatGPT OAuth flow (#614) is shipping and minting the duplicate identity in real configs; the picker clip is the #628 family still alive in this widget.

## Why this framing
- Two defects, one card, because both are picker-identity surface: the duplicate poisons "which provider am I on" (the same session later hit #705's switch bug), and the unreachable top makes the correct entry unselectable even when it exists.

## Architecture
- **Identity canonicalization** (subject: provider records): one canonical id per auth domain; an alias map folds `chatgpt.com` → `chatgpt` (and future domains). The OAuth write path RESOLVES aliases onto the existing entry instead of minting a new record. Invariant: *one provider id per auth domain across config, registry, and picker*.
- **Migration** (subject: already-split user configs): on load, duplicate same-domain records merge onto the canonical id — models and keys unioned, nothing dropped, a named note logged.
- **Picker viewport** (subject: the /model list widget): max height follows the live terminal size; ↑/↓ past the visible window scrolls so every entry is reachable. Invariant: *every listed entry is focusable by keys alone*. Codex reference for provider identity handling: https://github.com/openai/codex.

## Acceptance criteria (testable)
- **AC1** (RED, IT): fixture config with both `chatgpt` and `chatgpt.com` → load dedupes to one entry; the picker shows exactly one `· current`. (IT-D1)
- **AC2** (RED, IT): completing ChatGPT OAuth with an existing same-domain entry creates NO second record (alias resolution on the write path). (IT-D2)
- **AC3** (RED, E2E): /model with more entries than the window height — PTY test drives ↑/↓ past the fold; every entry reachable and selectable. (E2E-V1)
- **AC4** (REG): #614 auth-lands-in-list behavior, #628 clipping fixes, the #705 switch repro — all green. *Red REG blocks merge.* (REG-S1..S3)

## Test plan
### Test matrix
- `UT-D1..D3` — alias map resolution, merge rules (union of models/keys, conflict = canonical wins + note), canonical-id selection order: pure, no IO.
- `IT-D1..D2` — fixture configs through the real loader/registry (fakes, deterministic).
- `E2E-V1` — PTY: window height 12, 40 providers — every row focusable; selection lands on the canonical entry.
- `REG-S1..S3` — #614/#698-family auth flows, #628 pickers, provider switch path.

### Edge / border cases
- **E1** — split records carry DIFFERENT model lists: union, no loss; conflicting values resolve to canonical with a logged note.
- **E2** — the user's saved "current provider" points at the alias: resolves to canonical on load (no dangling pointer).
- **E3** — degenerate terminal (height < 3): picker still functional (min viewport + scroll), never a crash.
- **E4** — picker opened while a stream is in progress: list interaction never races the running turn's provider pointer.

## Non-goals
- Renaming/retheming the picker UI beyond the scroll fix.
- Cross-MACHINE identity sync (hub concerns stay out).
- Merging DIFFERENT auth domains (epam-copilot vs personal stay distinct — they are distinct).

## Open questions
- Canonical id spelling: `chatgpt` (current display) vs `chatgpt.com` (domain-shaped)? I lean `chatgpt` — shorter, already user-facing.

## References
#705 (same session's 400 — the downstream symptom), #614 (auth in one list), #628 (clipping family), codex: https://github.com/openai/codex.

{"content":"🚨 **BLOCKING: Merge notes are written to stdout — corrupts the HEP event stream and headless output**

```dart
customProviders: CustomProviderRegistry(saved.customProviders)
  ..mergeNotes.forEach(stdout.writeln),
```

`_runApp` also serves headless runs. With `--output events` (HEP v1, issue #155) stdout is a **strict JSONL stream** owned by `HepWriter` — the code right above this hunk says it verbatim: *"Stdout purity: deltas ride frames; diagnostics keep their channel"* (bin/fah.dart:1827-1830) and wraps `io` in `HepEventsIO` for exactly this reason. Any user whose saved config still carries a `chatgpt` + `chatgpt.com` split (the exact users this PR migrates) will get raw prose lines injected into the JSONL stream, breaking every server-side supervisor parsing it. Even plain headless `fa "prompt"` gets the note prepended to the answer stream.

The file already has the correct convention a few hundred lines up (bin/fah.dart:498):

```dart
void writeln(String text) =>
    headless ? stderr.writeln(text) : stdout.writeln(text);
```

Route the notes through `io`/stderr (or buffer them and emit through the CLI's diagnostic channel after `io` is built) instead of raw `stdout`.
","path":"outputs/pr_review_comments/comment1.md"}

{"content":"⚠️ **IMPORTANT: Merge note names the wrong survivor when the reserved ghost is listed first**

```dart
notes.add(
  'merged duplicate provider record "${entry.name}" onto "$first" '
  '(same auth domain)',
);
```

`_loadMergeNotes` assumes the FIRST-seen record is the survivor, but `_mergedOnLoad` has the reserved-ghost flip: for the config order `[chatgpt (reserved ghost), chatgpt.com]`, the survivor is **`chatgpt.com`** (non-reserved wins) and `chatgpt` is dropped — yet the note prints `merged duplicate provider record "chatgpt.com" onto "chatgpt"`, the exact opposite of what happened.

This note is the only audit trail of a migration that is persisted back to the user's config on the next save (the registry list is the live, persisted list), and these notes are now surfaced at every boot. Telling the user the wrong record survived sends them hunting for a `chatgpt.com` entry that no longer exists.

Two suggestions:
1. Emit the note from `_mergedOnLoad` itself, where the actual survivor is known — that also removes the duplicated detection pass (`_loadMergeNotes` re-implements the same grouping and can drift from `_mergedOnLoad`).
2. Add a test for the ghost-first order; the current tests only cover ghost-second.

{"content":"⚠️ **IMPORTANT: Alias landing ignores apiType/baseUrl — can overwrite an unrelated key slot and leave an inconsistent record**

```dart
final existing = registry != null
    ? (_entryForBaseUrl(registry, spec.defaultBaseUrl) ??
          _entryForCanonicalName(registry, spec.name))
    : null;
```

`_entryForCanonicalName` matches purely on the NAME (`canonicalProviderName(entry.name) == 'chatgpt'`). A user who hand-created an entry literally named `chatgpt.com` pointing at a **different** backend (a corporate proxy/relay, apiType `openai`, its own `keyName` slot) hits this path:

1. `existing` = the proxy entry → `keyName = existing.keyName` → `_storeProviderToken` **overwrites the proxy's stored key** with the ChatGPT OAuth blob (silent credential loss).
2. The in-place update below refreshes only `modelId`/`keyName` (lines 1416-1418) — the record keeps apiType `openai` and the proxy `baseUrl` while now holding Codex OAuth credentials that need the Responses-API dialect (`store: false`, `ChatGPT-Account-ID`). Switching to that entry later is broken in both directions.
3. `sameAccount = name == existing.name` is true, so the model pick is skipped for what may be a completely different account.

The doc comment ("may carry a variant base URL — landing on it is the point") shows this was considered, but the variant should still be constrained to the same auth domain: require `apiType == spec.name` (or a trailing-slash-normalized baseUrl match) before treating the record as the OAuth landing target, and/or refresh `apiType`/`baseUrl` on the target when landing. A proxy entry named `chatgpt.com` is exactly the kind of hand-edit this PR's migration is meant to clean up after.
","path":"outputs/pr_review_comments/comment3.md"}

{"content":"⚠️ **IMPORTANT: The `-9` chrome reserve doesn't account for group-header rows — the top-crop bug survives for grouped menus**

```dart
final maxVisible = (termHeight - 9).clamp(1, 6);
```

The reserve covers title + both hints + the models footer, but `_menuReservedLines` (same file, ~line 530) counts one more row per visible **group header** (`_groupHeadersIn`). `_menuWindow` is shared by every menu, and the slash menu renders groups (`commands`, `skills` — see `slash_menu.dart`), the composer overlay uses `paths`. With a grouped menu in a short terminal the frame still overruns the glass by the header count and `_cropToGlass` (line ~2165) drops rows from the TOP again — the same #706/#628 defect this PR fixes for the (ungrouped) /model picker.

The height math already exists and stays in sync with the renderer precisely because it lives in one place (`_menuReservedLines`: *"the height math and the renderer must agree"*). Consider computing the cap from that same accounting — e.g. clamp the window so `1 + window + headers(window) + hints + footer <= termHeight - fixedChrome` — instead of hand-mirroring the row budget in a magic `9` that will silently rot the next time the frame chrome changes.

💡 **SUGGESTION: The union-path assertion doesn't exercise the union — and the twin's modelId drop deserves a pinned decision**

```dart
expect(merged.keyName, isNotNull);
```

The survivor (`chatgpt.com`) already carries `keyName: 'FA_KEY_CHATGPT_COM_WORK'`, so `_unionOnto` never fires here — the assertion passes trivially and the actual union branch (survivor keyName null → inherit twin's slot) is untested. The test comment also overclaims: *"the union keeps the key slot and the last-used models"* — but `modelId` conflicts keep only the survivor's value, so the ghost's last-used model (`gpt-5`) and its key slot (`CHATGPT_OAUTH_CREDENTIALS`, which may still hold a live OAuth blob in the secure store) are silently dropped/orphaned.

Ticket E1 ("split records carry DIFFERENT model lists: union, no loss") is only half-covered: the picker's folded candidates do union the display side via the canonical fold, but the persisted record loses the twin's fields. Suggest:

1. A case where the survivor has `keyName: null` to pin the inherit behavior.
2. A case asserting which twin values are dropped (modelId conflict, second keyName) so the "conflicts keep survivor's" policy is explicit, and ideally surfacing the dropped key slot name in the merge note so the user can clean up the orphaned credential.

💡 **SUGGESTION: Alias-aware `find()` invalidates the "never collide with catalog names" invariant — update the stale contract comment**

A few lines below (`_handleProviderCommand`, ~line 530):

```dart
// A saved custom provider name resolves before the catalog (registry
// names can never collide with catalog names by construction).
final saved = args.length == 1
    ? config.customProviders?.find(args[0])
    : null;
```

With the alias fallback added to `CustomProviderRegistry.find` in this PR, `find('chatgpt')` now returns the saved `chatgpt.com` entry — so `/provider chatgpt` switches to the **saved entry** instead of the catalog provider. Registry names can now effectively collide with catalog names through the alias map, and the "by construction" invariant (also relied upon in AGENTS.md: *"`/provider kimi` routes to the catalog before the registry lookup, so such an entry would be unreachable"*) no longer holds for aliased domains.

The new routing is arguably the desired one-identity behavior — but it's an unannounced semantic change hiding behind a comment that still claims it can't happen. Please update the comment (and the AGENTS.md note if intentional), and consider a test pinning `/provider chatgpt` → saved-entry routing so a future alias-map entry doesn't silently hijack another catalog command.

Read input context:
instruction.md, ticket.md, pr_info.md,

re-read changed files,
surface ALL remaining issues"] EXHAUST --> OUTPUT["8. Write outputs:
pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Impact analysis (CodeGraph or grep fallback) Use CodeGraph to find "what could break": - `codegraph_callers` / `codegraph_callees` on modified public symbols - `codegraph_search` for: `PAT_TOKEN`, `secrets.`, `github.token`, `previousViewModel` - `codegraph_impact` before flagging architectural changes **If CodeGraph unavailable**, use grep and document it: ```bash grep -rn "changedFunctionName" --include="*.ts" . grep -rn "secrets\.\|github\.token" . ``` ## 5. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. # AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/unattended), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.
- `lib/src/tools/checkpoint_tool.dart` — `checkpoint`/`rewind` tools:
  context hygiene for detours. `CheckpointRewindController` wraps
  `Agent.prepareNextTurn`, persists via host `CheckpointSessionSink`.
  Lifecycle (issue #286): a checkpoint is scoped to its detour — when the
  next `checkpoint` call finds it stale (a user turn arrived inside the
  detour, or the anchored span was rebuilt away by reload/compaction), it
  is auto-closed with a note + `checkpoint_auto_closed` session record
  instead of refusing; `rewind` semantics are unchanged.
- `lib/src/compaction/branch_summarization.dart` — `generateBranchSummary` +
  `navigateSessionTree` (use instead of `Session.moveTo` for tree
  navigation); summary is a `branch_summary` record on the entered branch.
- `lib/src/agent/tool_pairing.dart` — context pair-integrity (issue #85):
  `validateToolPairing` checks the wire-equivalent message sequence (orphan
  results, unanswered calls, duplicate ids, displaced results after
  same-role merges); `repairToolPairing` fixes the outbound payload only
  (drop orphan + note, synthesize interrupted results, hoist steering text
  after results, uniquify duplicate ids symmetrically on call+result).
  `agent_loop.dart` repairs before every request and retries once on a
  pairing-shaped provider 400 (`ToolPairingRepairEvent` is the audit
  trail); `_finishStreamed` stamps per-run position-counter ids
  session-unique; `auto_compactor.dart`'s `_localTrimFallback` routes the
  kept region through the same repairer.
- `lib/src/agent/image_registry.dart` — session image registry (issue
  #171): unique images ride a provider request exactly once; every other
  occurrence becomes a `[Image N]` text ref. `rewriteHistoryImages`
  rewrites the OUTBOUND payload only (session JSONL byte-identical);
  carriers `[{text:"[Image N]"},{image}]` anchor before the first
  referencing user message or after the tool-result run (never inside
  call/result pairs); the current user message rides images in place
  (I3), each in-place image carrying its `[Image N]` label (issue #195
  F3 — the model can cite what it sees); the per-request cap
  (`images.maxPerRequest`, default 20) drops current-first-then-newest
  with a drop notice (never silent; the app logs drops via `AppLog`,
  issue #195 F4); dangling refs (compaction, cap) resolve to `(image no
  longer available)`, and once a renumbering boundary exists (compaction
  summary, structured marker, local-trim note) AUTHORED history
  citations degrade to that note too — after renumbering an `[Image N]`
  may name a different image, so silent rebinding is never allowed
  (issue #195 F2; generated refs/labels stay content-keyed and fresh).
  Stateless per-request rebuild — determinism, compaction eviction and
  resume come free. Kill switch `images.registry: false` → byte-for-byte
  legacy shape. `agent_loop.dart` applies it in `_buildRequestContext`
  after `transformContext`, before tool-pairing repair.
- `lib/src/trajectory/` — the trajectory ledger core (issue #10): finalized
  session records project into an immutable `TrajectorySnapshot` through
  `TrajectorySnapshotBuilder.append`/`applyEvent` — streamed agent events
  land as synthetic rows keyed `turn\0step` (`u\0turn` for prompts) and are
  replaced when the real record lands; revision grows per append. Record
  kinds (closed set, `TrajectoryCellKind`): system, user, context,
  compacted, message, tool, subtool — a subtool is a
  `TrajectoryToolRecord.parentCallId != null`, which only hosts build
  directly (the builder never nests). Derived state folds once per
  snapshot: `deriveTrajectoryLayout` (turns of Message/Step groups +
  collapsible turn/assistant-run summaries), `deriveTrajectoryTimeline`
  (four modes — `sequence` equal-width slots, `duration` with idle gaps
  compressed out, `time` zero-width wall-clock markers, `actual` real gaps;
  three fixed lanes: 0 system/user/context, 1 message/compacted, 2 tools),
  `trajectoryTimelineFocusIndexes` (selection → visible ledger indexes),
  and `ThrottledTrajectorySearchIndex` (full-text; matches are stable
  record ids). `formatters.dart` holds the shared duration/token/throughput
  formatting; `trajectory_preview.dart` the bounded single-line previews;
  `trajectory_export.dart` the whole-snapshot JSON/Markdown exporters the
  header's copy menu uses. Tool records carry `startedAt` (real launch
  time, distinct from the projected position) so the Gantt/actual
  projections plot true spans. Outbound model requests persist for the
  ledger as hidden `model_request_summary` `CustomRecord`s — the CLI
  event handler (`agent_event_handler.dart`, emitted through
  `agent_cli.dart`) and the app's `AgentService` both buffer a
  `TrajectoryRequestDetail` per call and flush it onto the session
  record chain right before the assistant message, so replays see it
  ahead of the reply — and `TrajectorySnapshotBuilder` folds them into
  the message record's request detail (the Request tab).
  Consumers render, never re-derive: `packages/fa_ui`'s
  `lib/src/trajectory/` widgets and the CLI `/trajectory` family.
- `lib/src/cli/trajectory_commands.dart` (a `part of` `agent_cli.dart`) +
  `lib/src/cli/trajectory_tui.dart` — the read-only REPL family
  `/trajectory [view|cost|tail|inspect <n>]` (bare = `view`, capped at 200
  rows; `tail` follows the live session every 500ms) and the headless
  `fa trajectory <view|tail|cost|inspect> [sessionId] [--json] [--at N]`
  subcommand (`--at N` replays the snapshot as it stood at record N, view
  only). Session resolution: exact id > session-name match > most recent.
  Rendering is pure Dart in `trajectory_tui.dart` (no `dart:io`), shared by
  both entries; `bin/fah.dart` routes the subcommand.

- **PR #**: 712
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/712
- **Title**: fix(706): /model picker — one ChatGPT identity, reachable list top
- **Author**: vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit
- **Branch**: `fix/706-model-picker-dupes` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 7
- **Additions**: +511
- **Deletions**: -32
- **Created**: 2026-09-19T21:56:50Z
- **Updated**: 2026-09-20T07:48:11Z

## PR Description

Fixes #706

## What was wrong
- **Twin identities, both "current"**: ChatGPT OAuth derives the account name from the endpoint host (`chatgpt.com`) while the catalog/active provider is `chatgpt` — the /model provider step listed both rows, each marked `· current` (one via the active custom entry, one via the active provider).
- **Unreachable list top**: the menu window was a fixed 6 items regardless of terminal height; in short terminals the frame overran the glass and `_cropToGlass` (#503 guard) dropped rows from the TOP — the picker title and first items became selectable-but-invisible while the `↑ more` hint below stayed painted.

## Delivered
- `providerNameAliases` (`chatgpt.com` → `chatgpt`) + `canonicalProviderName()` in `custom_providers.dart`.
- Load-time migration: `CustomProviderRegistry` merges same-auth-domain records onto one (field union, reserved-named ghosts yield to non-reserved twins, named notes in `registry.mergeNotes`, surfaced at boot in `bin/fah.dart`).
- Alias-aware `registry.find()`.
- OAuth write path (`_applyChatGptOAuthCredentials`): resolves the existing same-domain record (base URL **or** canonical-name alias) and lands on it in place — no second record; the name prompt allows the alias-resolved target.
- Picker fold: `_modelProviderNames`/`_crossProviderCandidates`/`_providerModelCount`/`_openProviderModelPicker` group domain twins into ONE row (saved-entry spelling wins); the current marker compares canonical ids — exactly one `· current`.
- Viewport: `_menuWindow()` caps the window to the terminal height (`min(6, termHeight - 9)`, floor 1) so title + first items always land on the glass; tall terminals keep the classic 6-row window and hints.

## Tests (failing-first)
- `test/cli/agent_cli_provider_identity_test.dart` (3): load-merge of split records; full headless-OAuth repro of the owner screenshot → exactly one chatgpt identity row and exactly one current marker; OAuth onto an existing same-domain record mints no second record (blob lands in that record's key slot).
- `test/cli/fa_tui_picker_viewport_test.dart` (3): pgup lands title+first row on the glass in a 10-row terminal (was cropped: reproduced the exact reported frame); every row visible while walking a 12-item list at height 12; 24-row terminal keeps the legacy 6-row window + both hints.
- Regression zones green: agent_cli_model, agent_cli_provider, agent_cli_chatgpt_oauth, custom_providers, fa_tui, add_provider_picker, tui adapter/mouse/sync, aiin/copilot/env-preconfig/folder-model/compact/ext provider flows, codemie_sso_server, config_service — 325 passing.

## Gate note
`dart analyze` cannot run inside this `.worktrees/` lane under the current cube policy (analysis-server path canonicalization EPERMs — same family the chief flagged); the equivalent gates ran instead: harness Dart analysis server diagnostics clean on all 7 touched files, `dart format` applied, and every touched file compiled + exercised by the targeted suites above.

## Remaining (out of scope here)
- AC3's PTY-driven E2E variant (the model-level key-path tests cover the same interaction; the pty2 harness exists for a follow-up if wanted).
- Multi-row composer drafts while the picker is open can still squeeze the frame beyond the window cap (single-row draft — the picker reality — is covered).
- A `chatgpt-codex.com`-style future domains just need one map entry in `providerNameAliases`.

# gh-706: [BUG] /model picker: duplicate ChatGPT provider identities both marked current + list top unreachable ('↑ more' but no scroll)

## Description

## Goal — one provider identity, a fully reachable picker (v1, full create-goal rewrite)

One sentence: **every auth domain owns exactly one provider entry, and every model in the /model picker is reachable** — no `chatgpt` + `chatgpt.com` twins both marked "current", no `↑ more` rows the keys cannot reach.

Today (owner screenshot, 2026-09-19): the CLI /model picker lists both `chatgpt.com 1 model(s) · current` and `chatgpt 1 model(s) · current` — two identities for one ChatGPT auth — and the top of the list sits behind an `↑ more` marker that scrolling cannot actually reach. Why now: the ChatGPT OAuth flow (#614) is shipping and minting the duplicate identity in real configs; the picker clip is the #628 family still alive in this widget.

## Why this framing
- Two defects, one card, because both are picker-identity surface: the duplicate poisons "which provider am I on" (the same session later hit #705's switch bug), and the unreachable top makes the correct entry unselectable even when it exists.

## Architecture
- **Identity canonicalization** (subject: provider records): one canonical id per auth domain; an alias map folds `chatgpt.com` → `chatgpt` (and future domains). The OAuth write path RESOLVES aliases onto the existing entry instead of minting a new record. Invariant: *one provider id per auth domain across config, registry, and picker*.
- **Migration** (subject: already-split user configs): on load, duplicate same-domain records merge onto the canonical id — models and keys unioned, nothing dropped, a named note logged.
- **Picker viewport** (subject: the /model list widget): max height follows the live terminal size; ↑/↓ past the visible window scrolls so every entry is reachable. Invariant: *every listed entry is focusable by keys alone*. Codex reference for provider identity handling: https://github.com/openai/codex.

## Acceptance criteria (testable)
- **AC1** (RED, IT): fixture config with both `chatgpt` and `chatgpt.com` → load dedupes to one entry; the picker shows exactly one `· current`. (IT-D1)
- **AC2** (RED, IT): completing ChatGPT OAuth with an existing same-domain entry creates NO second record (alias resolution on the write path). (IT-D2)
- **AC3** (RED, E2E): /model with more entries than the window height — PTY test drives ↑/↓ past the fold; every entry reachable and selectable. (E2E-V1)
- **AC4** (REG): #614 auth-lands-in-list behavior, #628 clipping fixes, the #705 switch repro — all green. *Red REG blocks merge.* (REG-S1..S3)

## Test plan
### Test matrix
- `UT-D1..D3` — alias map resolution, merge rules (union of models/keys, conflict = canonical wins + note), canonical-id selection order: pure, no IO.
- `IT-D1..D2` — fixture configs through the real loader/registry (fakes, deterministic).
- `E2E-V1` — PTY: window height 12, 40 providers — every row focusable; selection lands on the canonical entry.
- `REG-S1..S3` — #614/#698-family auth flows, #628 pickers, provider switch path.

### Edge / border cases
- **E1** — split records carry DIFFERENT model lists: union, no loss; conflicting values resolve to canonical with a logged note.
- **E2** — the user's saved "current provider" points at the alias: resolves to canonical on load (no dangling pointer).
- **E3** — degenerate terminal (height < 3): picker still functional (min viewport + scroll), never a crash.
- **E4** — picker opened while a stream is in progress: list interaction never races the running turn's provider pointer.

## Non-goals
- Renaming/retheming the picker UI beyond the scroll fix.
- Cross-MACHINE identity sync (hub concerns stay out).
- Merging DIFFERENT auth domains (epam-copilot vs personal stay distinct — they are distinct).

## Open questions
- Canonical id spelling: `chatgpt` (current display) vs `chatgpt.com` (domain-shaped)? I lean `chatgpt` — shorter, already user-facing.

## References
#705 (same session's 400 — the downstream symptom), #614 (auth in one list), #628 (clipping family), codex: https://github.com/openai/codex.

## Automated Code Review — BLOCK

**Summary**: The identity canonicalization (alias map, load-time merge, alias-aware `find`, picker fold) and the viewport cap correctly address both halves of #706 — the 6 new tests pass locally, `dart analyze` is clean on all touched files, and regression suites are green. However, the boot merge notes are printed to raw `stdout` inside `_runApp`, which corrupts the strict-JSONL HEP stream (`--output events`) and headless answers for exactly the users being migrated — this must be fixed before merge.

**Key Issues**:
- 🚨 BLOCKING — `bin/fah.dart:1888`: `mergeNotes.forEach(stdout.writeln)` violates stdout purity in headless/HEP mode; use the stderr/diagnostic channel (precedent at `bin/fah.dart:498`).
- ⚠️ IMPORTANT — `custom_providers.dart:275`: merge note names the wrong survivor when the reserved ghost is listed first (note says folded onto `chatgpt`, but `chatgpt.com` survives) — the only audit trail of a persisted config rewrite.
- ⚠️ IMPORTANT — `provider_commands.dart:1358`: alias landing matches on name only; a same-named entry on a different backend (proxy) gets its key slot overwritten with the OAuth blob and keeps a stale `apiType`/`baseUrl`.
- ⚠️ IMPORTANT — `fa_tui.dart:513`: the `-9` reserve ignores group-header rows (`_groupHeadersIn`), so grouped menus (slash menu) can still overrun the glass and trip the top-crop in short terminals.
- 💡 2 suggestions: union path not actually exercised by the test (twin's modelId/key slot silently dropped); alias-aware `find()` makes the "registry names never collide with catalog" comment at `provider_commands.dart:531` stale (`/provider chatgpt` now routes to the saved entry).

**Ticket check**: AC1/AC2 covered by the new integration tests; AC4 regression zones green per PR description. AC3's PTY-driven E2E is explicitly deferred (noted as remaining work in the PR) — acceptable if tracked, since the model-level key-path tests cover the same interaction.

**Next Steps**:
1. Route merge notes to stderr/the CLI diagnostic channel instead of `stdout`.
2. Fix the merge-note survivor direction (emit from `_mergedOnLoad`) and add the ghost-first test.
3. Constrain `_entryForCanonicalName` to the same auth domain (apiType/baseUrl) or refresh `apiType`/`baseUrl` on the in-place landing.
4. Derive the picker window cap from the `_menuReservedLines` accounting so group headers can't reopen the top-crop.

re-read changed files,
surface ALL remaining issues"] EXHAUST --> OUTPUT["8. Write outputs:
pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Impact analysis (CodeGraph or grep fallback) Use CodeGraph to find "what could break": - `codegraph_callers` / `codegraph_callees` on modified public symbols - `codegraph_search` for: `PAT_TOKEN`, `secrets.`, `github.token`, `previousViewModel` - `codegraph_impact` before flagging architectural changes **If CodeGraph unavailable**, use grep and document it: ```bash grep -rn "changedFunctionName" --include="*.ts" . grep -rn "secrets\.\|github\.token" . ``` ## 5. Review dimensions Rate the PR across all relevant dimensions: | Dimension | What to check | |---|---| | **Security** | injection, unsafe interpolation, secret leakage, missing permissions, unsafe defaults | | **Architecture / OOP** | SRP, coupling, abstraction consistency, provider/repository boundaries | | **Code quality** | naming, complexity, error handling, logging, comments | | **Tests** | coverage for new/changed paths, meaningful assertions, no brittle string-only tests | | **Duplication** | copy-paste, duplicated logic across files, duplicated configuration | | **Backward compatibility** | public API changes, migration paths, default behavior | | **Performance** | unnecessary rebuilds, heavy sync operations, missing timeouts | | **Workflow / CI safety** | (when `.github/workflows/` changes) secret declarations, ref pinning, permissions, timeouts | ## 6.
